method_description: Per-paper generate -> critique -> narrow (loop.md 28.1, 28.3). For the research question, the 10 most relevant papers published before the knowledge cutoff are retrieved. For each paper, o3-mini writes 3 hypotheses that build on it, using teaching-text passages and MatKG facts as background; a critic (o3-mini, high reasoning effort) that sees the paper and background but never the question checks each for soundness, testability and going beyond the paper; the generator revises until at least one is accepted (at most 20 rounds, else the paper is dropped). The accepted hypotheses of all papers, near-duplicates merged, meet in a pairwise tournament on the question (o3-mini, high effort; both orders, a win needs both). Rank 1 is the final hypothesis.

broad.question: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

problem_constrained.question: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

expert_context.question: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.
